oracle_model.description: The input is available through a coherent indexed bit or phase query.

signal.definition: The signature is sqrt(w(x)/n), equal to the nonzero singular value of [x_1 ... x_n]/sqrt(n).
signal.normalization: The row operator has Euclidean norm at most one.

readout.rule: Return one iff the singular-value signature is positive.

cost.construction: Prepare a uniform index state and apply one coherent input query to create the marked component.
assumptions: Uniform index-state preparation is not counted as an input query.
This record does not include the polynomial-filter or amplification degree.

limitations: The record does not by itself prove optimal query complexity or advantage.

promise_domain.description: All five-bit strings; odd width removes the tie case.

oracle_model.description: The input is available through a coherent indexed bit or phase query.

readout.rule: Return one iff the normalized Hamming signal is positive.

cost.construction: Use a uniform index register and an indexed phase query to block encode the average signed bit observable.
assumptions: One signal call means one invocation of the block-encoding primitive, not classical computation of Hamming weight.
State preparation and reflection costs must be added in later resource work packages.

limitations: The adjacent-class gap scales as 2/n without a stronger margin promise.
Finite-domain separation does not establish a low fault-tolerant gate count.

oracle_model.description: The input is available through a coherent indexed bit or phase query.

readout.rule: Return one iff the phase signature is -1.

cost.construction: Accumulate the XOR of all four queried bits into a phase.
assumptions: Exact construction under the bit-query model queries every bit in this fixture.
The constant-dimensional signal is intentionally retained as an access-cost control.

limitations: Perfect label separation is purchased by full-input access.
This candidate demonstrates that signal dimension alone is not an algorithmic complexity measure.

oracle_model.description: The input is available through a coherent indexed bit or phase query.

signal.definition: The signature is 2w(x)/n - 1, while labels are parity.

readout.rule: Any exact scalar polynomial readout must alternate at every consecutive Hamming weight.
readout.zero_region: Signals associated with even Hamming weights.
readout.one_region: Signals associated with odd Hamming weights.

cost.construction: Use a uniform index register and an indexed phase query to block encode the average signed bit observable.
assumptions: The signal primitive is cheap, but the required polynomial is highly oscillatory.
The alternation count is only a degree lower bound for exact sign realization on sampled points.

limitations: No low-degree exact scalar separator exists across all five ordered Hamming signals.
The fixture does not substitute for the general polynomial or adversary lower-bound methods.
